Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. We ran an internal spike overnight and the results look promising. Starlight Labs is preparing an enterprise contract and procurement asked whether Redwood can commit to a response-floor for our user-facing inference endpoint during peak hours. Specifically:

- Commitment asked: median (p50) < 70ms and a 95th percentile (p95) bound of < 140ms for the embeddings/classification endpoint during our defined business hours (PST 14:00–22:00).
- Expected sustained QPS: 220–350 during peaks; spiky bursts up to ~700 for short periods (2–5min).
- Traffic mix: 60% short (<=128 tokens) classification calls, 40% embedding vector generation and similarity lookups.

We understand these are tighter than standard. Procurement also asked for an operational fallback plan and an SLA definition (how are you measuring p95, what counts as incident). They want this codified in the MSA appendix.

Attaching our summary spreadsheet (starlight_requested_sla.xlsx). Can you confirm feasibility and next steps? Jordan Park (cc'd) is the procurement lead.

Appreciate it —
Alex

Thanks — a few contract/ops notes up front:

- Definition: We must be explicit whether p95 is measured at the token-level, request-level, or end-to-end (including network). My preference: request-level end-to-end from our ingress to final token emitted for the single outstanding request.
- Measurement window: agree a 30-day rolling window for SLA evaluation and clarify sampling methodology and what telemetry (traces/metrics) will be shared.
- Remedy: performance-credit ladder tied to % miss against the committed p95; limit exposure to X% of monthly bill (we can propose numbers once engineering scopes the risk).
- Operational fallback: we need an automatic, documented fallback (route to a compatible but lower-cost model variant or degrade non-critical features) before we take credit liability. This must be in the appendix.

I'll draft suggested appendix language. Also want to run the traffic profile past Security — any data retention or network egress concerns? Mina, can you check?

-Laura
Head of Customer Ops/Contracts

Feasibility notes — technical:

Short answer: achievable with constraints and a dedicated pool + runbook, but p95 < 140ms for mixed embedding+classification at sustained 350 QPS is aggressive and depends on model size and token lengths. Details:

- Model sizing: if we serve a ~7B architecture optimized for embeddings with quantization and memory-friendly kernels we can hit sub-100ms p50 and likely p95 ~120–160ms under good cache hit rates. Larger models push tail up. Need Starlight to commit to the model family/weights (no frequent model switches).
- Warmup & cache: require an onboarding warm-up to populate KV caches and prefix caches. Recommend a 24–48 hour warm period with synthetic traffic replay and progressive ramp.
- Dedicated routing: affinity routing to pinned GPUs (no noisy neighbors), plus an autoscale buffer of 20% headroom. For bursts, a reserved burst queue with pre-allocated warm workers avoids cold-start spikes.
- Instrumentation: we will provide request-level tracing (trace id) + sample payloads in a shared monitoring dashboard. Need to agree on retention for traces used to adjudicate SLOs.
- Measurement: we measure p95 at the request completion time at our egress. We need an agreed timestamping method to avoid clock skew disputes.

Open asks for Starlight:
1) Confirm model family + whether they accept a quantized variant (might degrade quality for embeddings).
2) Provide production traffic replay logs for 2 full workdays so we can simulate load.

I can put together a runbook and perf checklist. If legal wants to cap exposure, we should quantify expected miss probability from simulations.

-Aditya
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

- We believe we can support a bounded response-floor for Starlight with a Dedicated reserved pool + burst capacity and a 24–48 hour warm-up run, provided you commit to the model family and a 12-month reserved capacity (we'll quote two sizing options).
- Proposed interim SLO (for contract appendix): request-level p50 < 80ms and p95 <= 160ms during the defined business hours, measured at Redwood egress on a 30-day rolling window. We're prioritizing a conservative commitment for sign-off; final numbers will be calibrated after the load replay and a warm-up run.
- Required next steps from Starlight: 48 hours of production-like traffic replay, confirmation of model family, and acceptance of a short onboarding fee to cover pre-warm and extra engineering time.

Attached: SLA_proposal_v0.2.pdf (initial appendix language + measurement definitions). Karthik will follow up on commercial terms and credit caps. Laura will lead appendix redlines. Aditya will schedule a perf-sim run once we have replay data.

Can you confirm you can provide the replay by EOD Jul 13? If yes, I'll lock a preliminary go/no-go meeting for Jul 14 with Eng/Product/Contracts to sign off and generate a draft appendix for procurement.

Best —
Marissa
